headline: Zoning changes on ADUs, parking, and class VI roads approved; Procopio agreement vote moved to November 9.
summary: Residents raised safety concerns about the Stokes Road bridge, and the chair plans a public hearing with the state transportation commissioner. Members also approved zoning changes that state law requires, and a Planning Board resignation was accepted.
decisions: Accepted the resignation of Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board.
Approved zoning changes on accessory dwelling units, residential parking, and class VI roads, 5-0.
Postponed the vote on the off-site improvement agreement with Procopio to the November 9 agenda, using council privilege.
discussion: Former town manager investigation: Public comment focused on two investigation reports about the former town manager and a lawsuit he filed over his firing.

Stokes Road bridge funding: Residents said the bridge is in worse shape than the Hall Road Bridge and asked for a safe way in and out. Members debated moving the state money back and agreed to more study and a public hearing with the state commissioner.

Parking rules for new homes: Residents and members asked whether one parking space per unit is safe for snow and emergency access. Staff said state law sets the one-space minimum and towns cannot require more.
Procopio agreement timing: Members said they had too little time to review the contract, which was sent out shortly before the meeting. Staff said the delay came from outside work on the project.
Public works facility plan: Members asked about salt storage, heating, and solar panels for a planned public works building. Members said more questions would come at a later meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: So moved. A motion from Ted. A second. A second from Deb. All those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. Any opposed? Shows affirmative.

I'll move that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the proposed amendments to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance related to accessory dwelling units pursuant to RSA 674:71-73, residential parking pursuant to RSA 674:16, Part VII, and development on class VI highways and private roads pursuant to RSA 674:41, as recommended by the planning board on September 2nd, 2026, and as presented...Shows in the affirmative, 5-0.
So, let the record show Councilor Bouchard does invoke council privilege. This will be on the November 9th agenda for a vote.
So moved. I have a motion from Ted. A second from Shawn. Any discussion? All those in favor, say aye. Aye. Any opposed? Chair votes in the affirmative.
